blockNote: Reset, main loop and sub-frame runners (file offsets 0-516, SNES $00:8000-$8204, bank 00).
=== FRAME MODEL ===

BootGame (the reset vector) sets native mode, D = 0, S = $1FFF and DBR = $01, runs the hardware init (code_0139AC), code_013ADA, code_027912 and code_0276EE (BG3 tilemap buffer), sets scene_next = $000C (scene 0C of area 0, the boot scene), enables NMI, calls the scene loader once and falls into RunMainLoop.
One pass of RunMainLoop is one game frame (location_id not $10-$12 and the low byte of return_active zero):
1. WaitVBlank (code_0131B7): NMI is on, so HandleVBlank runs inside this wait.
2. Scene loader code_027781, only when the low byte of scene_next is non-zero; it runs its own frames through RunSubFrameLoader.
3. Menu code_0118FC (Select or X) and pause code_027572 (Start), NMI still on.
4. DisableNmi (code_0131AE): everything below is the work phase and runs with NMI off.
5. code_0109D6 (return-point store), code_01185E (per-frame reset: HDMA shadow dp$42 = 0 and dp$44-dp$48).
6. RunActors, CullAndSortActors, DetectHitSourceCollisions, DetectPlayerContact, code_003005 (death check and automatic Medical Herb), code_010069 and code_01010B (scroll), BuildOamFromActors.
7. HUD (code_012659, code_011695), code_027223 (queues one animated tile strip), EnableNmi (code_0131A2), back to step 1.
=== VARIANTS ===

RunReducedLoop: location_id $10-$12 (unnamed scenes of the Up Above area, OQ-I001-6; the boot scene 00/0C should be location $12, OQ-I005-21). Runs DisableNmi, code_01185E, RunActors, CullAndSortActors, BuildOamFromActors and EnableNmi only: no menu, no hit tests, no HUD.

RunReturnLoop: low byte of return_active non-zero. Same as the main loop without menu, hit tests and scroll update, and Start, Select and X are cleared; after one frame it loops over RunSubFrame (WaitReturnDone) while bit 7 of $03FC is set, then adds player_max_hp / 8 to heal_pending, calls code_013140 with A = $78, sets transition_type = $80, copies return_area, return_scene, return_x and return_y into area_next, scene_next, warp_dest_x and warp_dest_y, enables NMI and jumps back to RunMainLoop (OQ-I005-17).
=== SUB-FRAMES ===

RunSubFrameLoader, RunSubFrameMapSweep and RunSubFrame run one complete game frame from inside a script, a menu, the text renderer or the scene loader. They set subframe_active ($03A6) to 1 while the work phase runs: RunActorList then runs only actors whose $16 bit $0010 is set, so a modal routine keeps its own actors alive while the rest of the game stands still. The player actor code and w2_actor_0FA6F5 also read $03A6.
=== WRAM ===

return_active $03FB (word read, low byte = flag), return_area $03FD, return_scene $03FF, return_x $0401, return_y $0403; scene_next $0318 (word) and area_next $0319; warp_dest_x $037C, warp_dest_y $037E; transition_type $03E3; heal_pending $043B; subframe_active $03A6; scene_loading $0462 (HUD skipped while non-zero in RunSubFrameLoader).
=== NOTES ===

- The three RunSubFrame* routines differ only in setup: RunSubFrameLoader disables NMI itself, calls the camera update code_010000 and skips the HUD while scene_loading is set; RunSubFrameMapSweep and RunSubFrame expect NMI off and set DBR = $01 (OQ-I005-20 asks whether every caller guarantees that).
- The extractor decodes code_01185E and code_01010B with the wrong M flag (OQ-I005-7); the callers run with M = 1.

BootGame: Reset vector: puts the machine in a known state and enters the main loop; never returns.
When: power on or reset (emulation-mode reset vector).
Sees: nothing until the first scene (scene_next = $000C) has loaded; then the boot scene (OQ-I005-21).
Why: native mode with D = 0, S = $1FFF and DBR = $01 (the bank the NMI and the loops assume), hardware init, then the scene loader builds the first scene.
Out: never returns; the loop runs with M = 1, X = 16-bit, D = 0, S = $1FFF, DBR = $01.
partNotes.RunMainLoop: One game frame (steps in the block note): wait for vblank, scene loader, menu and pause, then the work phase with NMI off. Entered from BootGame, RunReducedLoop and RunReturnLoop; every pass ends with EnableNmi and a jump back here.
RunReducedLoop: Frame for location_id $10-$12: actors, sort and OAM only (no menu, hit tests, HUD or return-point store).
When: every frame while location_id is $10, $11 or $12 (OQ-I005-21).
Sees: the scenes that need no player input handling (location $10 is where the title code runs; OQ-I001-6 leaves $11 and $12 open).
Why: those scenes have no player-driven combat or menu, so the loop skips that work.
RunReturnLoop: Frame while a return to the stored return point is pending (low byte of return_active non-zero).
When: return_active is set by actor scripts of worlds 2 and 3 (OQ-I005-17).

Sees: the world keeps animating without the player: Start, Select and X are cleared so the menu cannot open, and the HUD runs. When WaitReturnDone ends, the player is warped to return_area, return_scene, return_x, return_y.
Why: moves the player back to a saved place with a short heal (max HP / 8 added to heal_pending).
In: NMI on at the label; it disables it first.
partNotes.WaitReturnDone: Runs RunSubFrame while bit 7 of $03FC is set (word read of return_active), then finishes the return: clears return_active and $03FC, adds player_max_hp / 8 to heal_pending, runs code_013140 with A = $78, sets transition_type = $80, copies the return point into the next-scene variables and jumps to RunMainLoop with NMI on.
RunSubFrameLoader: Runs one complete game frame from inside the scene loader (and once from the menu code), then returns with NMI enabled.
When: 12 call sites in the scene loader and 1 in the menu code, usually to let actors, scroll and OAM advance while the scene is being built.
Sees: the scene appears and animates while the loader works (for example the iris transition).
Why: the loader cannot wait for the main loop, so it steps the frame itself.
In: any NMI state; M = 1; DBR kept. B, A (both bytes), X, Y and DBR are saved and restored.

Out: one vblank has passed, NMI on. subframe_active is 1 during the work phase and 0 on return. The HUD is skipped while scene_loading ($0462) is non-zero; the camera update code_010000 runs here only.
Clobbers: none visible; the callees use dp $00-$1C, $38-$3A and $42-$54.
RunSubFrameMapSweep: Runs one complete game frame with NMI off before and after, adding the map sweep redraw (code_010EEA).
When: 8 call sites in the return-point and lair-return code (code_0109D6, code_010EA9).
Sees: the map sweep effect that redraws the map while those routines run.
Why: lets the routine animate a multi-frame effect without leaving its own code.
In: NMI must be off (OQ-I005-20); M = 1; DBR is set to $01 and restored.
Out: one vblank passed; NMI off again. subframe_active is 1 during the work phase.
Clobbers: none visible (B, A, X, Y saved).
RunSubFrame: Runs one complete game frame with NMI off before and after (actors, sort, scroll, OAM, HUD, tile strip), without the map sweep.
When: 4 call sites: WaitReturnDone, the text renderer (twice) and one more routine (code_0126CF).
Sees: actors keep animating while text prints or a return waits.
Why: a routine that must wait several frames calls this instead of returning to the main loop.
In: NMI must be off (OQ-I005-20); M = 1; DBR is set to $01 and restored.
Out: one vblank passed; NMI off again. subframe_active is 1 during the work phase.
Clobbers: none visible (B, A, X, Y saved).

blockNote: NMI handler and the DMA routines it calls (file offsets 834-1444, SNES $00:8342-$85A4, bank 00).
=== ORDER OF WORK IN HandleVBlank ===

Saves P, B, A, X and Y; works with M = 1, X = 16-bit, DBR = $01. HDMAEN = 0; then DmaOamBuffer, DmaCgramAndFixedColor, DmaBg3TilemapPage, WriteScrollRegisters, UploadMapStripBuffers, DmaDynamicSpriteTiles, DmaAnimatedTileStrip, FlushVramWriteQueue and the title and file-select hook engine_title_file_select.code_006B7F; then wait for the auto-joypad read (HVBJOY bit 0); HDMAEN = dp$42 (the shadow the work phase set); frame_counter++; joypad; sound request. DMA channels: 0 = OAM, 1 = CGRAM, 2 = every VRAM transfer.
HandleIrq (the IRQ vector) is a bare RTI; the I flag is never cleared (no CLI in extracted/), so the IRQ stays masked.
=== JOYPAD ===

JOY1L is read as one word. The X button (word bit 6) is copied to the Select position (bit 13), so X and Select act as one button. joy_pressed = raw buttons with the bits of joy_block_mask removed (scripts block buttons with TSB and TRB on joy_block_mask), ANDed with joy_release_latch: a button counts only while its latch bit is set. The latch gets a bit whenever that button is seen up; the users (player code, menus, level up) clear the bit with TRB after using a press, so a held button acts once. Scene init sets the latch to $FFFF. joy_override ($0468) non-zero skips all of this and keeps the scripted value in joy_pressed (used by the Lisa and Turbo scene).
=== SOUND ===
sound_request ($0398, word) is filled by the BRK handler (native_mode_brk_0055FC): BRK #n requests sound n. On even frames the word goes to APUIO2 and is cleared; on odd frames 0 is sent.
=== STAGING DATA THE NMI UPLOADS ===
- oam_buffer $0486: 512 bytes low table + 32 bytes high table (544 bytes, channel 0 to OAMDATA).
- palette $7F0000 (512 bytes, channel 1 to CGDATA); COLDATA from coldata_buffer $7F0200-$7F0202.
- BG3 tilemap pages: $7F7000 to VRAM $5800, or (bit 1 of vram_upload_flags) $7F7800 to $5C00, 2048 bytes each.

- Scroll words: BG1 from scroll_bg1_x/y ($033A, $033C), BG2 from scroll_bg2_x/y ($033E, $0340), each value 10 bits (low byte, then high byte and 3); bg_scroll_swap ($03DB) non-zero swaps the pairs. BG3 uses the low bytes of scroll_bg3_x/y.
- Map strip records at $3000, $3102 and $3204, $3306 ($102 bytes each; column record, then row record).
- tile_dma_list $1A06: 3-byte records (source address word, bank), 0 ends; tile_dma_pending is the trigger.
- vram_strip_src, vram_strip_dest, vram_strip_pending ($03DD, $03DF, $03E1): one animated background strip.
- vram_write_queue $1C7B: pairs of words (VRAM address, data), address 0 ends.

HandleVBlank: NMI handler: uploads everything the work phase prepared, then reads the pad and sends the sound request.
When: every vblank while NMI is enabled (the main loop waits for it in WaitVBlank).
Sees: all graphics changes of a frame (sprites, palette, tilemap, scroll, animated tiles) appear here, and input and sound are sampled here.
Why: VRAM, CGRAM and OAM may only be written in vblank, and the work phase runs with NMI off, so the NMI is the single place that transfers the results.
In: hardware; saves P, B, A, X, Y; body runs with M = 1, X = 16-bit, DBR = $01.
Clobbers: none visible; writes dp $32-$37 through UploadMapStripBuffers.
partNotes.WaitAutoJoypad: Waits until the auto-joypad read has finished (HVBJOY bit 0 clear) before JOY1L is read; HDMAEN is restored from dp$42 right after this wait.
partNotes.StoreJoyPressed: Join point of the joypad code: stores A in joy_pressed. Reached by the normal path with the latched value and by the branch for joy_override with the scripted value.
partNotes.WriteSoundPort: Writes A (a sound request word on even frames, 0 on odd frames) to APUIO2, then restores the registers and returns with RTI.
DmaOamBuffer: Copies the 544-byte OAM buffer to OAM.
When: every NMI. Sees: the sprites built by BuildOamFromActors. Why: OAM can only be written in vblank.
Out: channel 0: 544 bytes ($0220) from oam_buffer ($0486) to OAMDATA, OAMADD = 0.
DmaCgramAndFixedColor: Copies the 512-byte palette buffer to CGRAM and writes the three fixed-colour components.
When: every NMI. Sees: palette changes and the fixed colour (screen tint). Why: the work phase edits the buffers, the NMI transfers them.
Out: channel 1: 512 bytes from $7F0000 to CGDATA with CGADD = 0; then $7F0200, $7F0201 and $7F0202 to COLDATA.
DmaBg3TilemapPage: Uploads one 2048-byte BG3 tilemap page (text and HUD layer) when vram_upload_flags asks for it.
When: every NMI; skipped when the high byte of the first write-queue word ($1C7C) is non-zero or vram_upload_flags is 0 (OQ-I005-19).
Sees: dialogue boxes and the HUD appear. Why: the text renderer draws into a staging page and flags it.
In: vram_upload_flags (bit 1 selects the second page).
Out: bit 1 clear: $7F7000 to VRAM $5800 and all flags cleared; bit 1 set: $7F7800 to $5C00 and only bit 1 cleared. Channel 2, 2048 bytes.
WriteScrollRegisters: Writes the BG1, BG2 and BG3 scroll registers.
When: every NMI. Sees: the camera. Why: scroll registers are written during vblank so a frame never mixes two positions.
In: scroll_bg3_x/y, the BG1 and BG2 scroll words, bg_scroll_swap ($03DB).
Out: BG3 gets the low byte of its scroll words (high byte 0); BG1 and BG2 are written through WriteScrollPair, with the two pairs swapped while bg_scroll_swap is non-zero.
WriteScrollPair: Writes one BG scroll pair (horizontal and vertical) with the 10-bit masking.
When: twice per NMI from WriteScrollRegisters. Why: every scroll register takes two writes (low byte, then high byte masked with 3).
In: X = offset into the scroll block (0 for BG1, 4 for BG2), Y = register pair (0 BG1, 2 BG2).
Out: BG1HOFS+Y and BG1VOFS+Y written twice each.
UploadMapStripBuffers: Uploads the two pairs of map strip records (new map columns and rows revealed by scrolling) to VRAM.
When: every NMI. Sees: the map drawing in as the camera moves. Why: the map is bigger than VRAM, so the edge strips are streamed in.
In: none. Sets dp$32 and dp$35 to the record pointers ($3000 and $3102, then $3204 and $3306); the bank bytes dp$34 and dp$37 are not set here.
Out: two calls of code_01057D; each uploads the column record (VMAIN $81) and the row record (VMAIN $80), four 64-byte blocks each, then zeroes the record's first word.
DmaDynamicSpriteTiles: Copies the tiles of dynamic-tile sprites into VRAM in two passes (top and bottom tile rows).

When: every NMI with tile_dma_pending non-zero (set by BuildActorSprites). Sees: actors flagged $1A bit $8000 (candidates: bosses and large monsters, OQ-I005-6) show their frames from streamed tiles. Why: those frames are copied into VRAM every frame.
In: tile_dma_list at $1A06: 3-byte records (source word, bank byte), 0 ends.
Out: pass 1 to VRAM $2000 upward (0x40 bytes per record); pass 2 adds $0200 to each record's source and uploads to $2100 upward; tile_dma_pending cleared. There is no count limit (OQ-I005-6).
DmaSpriteTileRecords: Uploads one 0x40-byte DMA per record of tile_dma_list until the terminator.
When: twice per NMI from DmaDynamicSpriteTiles. Why: shared loop of the two passes.
In: Y = list offset; DMAP2 and BBAD2 set by the caller; VMADDL set.
DmaAnimatedTileStrip: Uploads one animated background tile strip (two 0x40-byte blocks) to VRAM.
When: every NMI with vram_strip_pending non-zero (code_027223 sets it once per frame outside locations $0F-$12).
Sees: background tile animation (four VRAM slots cycling, 32 source frames).
Why: animates BG tiles without the work phase touching VRAM.
Out: 0x40 bytes to vram_strip_dest, the next 0x40 bytes to the address 256 words higher (high byte + 1); vram_strip_pending cleared.
FlushVramWriteQueue: Writes the queued (VRAM address, data) word pairs to VRAM and empties the queue.
When: every NMI, last of the transfers. Sees: single tilemap or tile edits (HUD digits, small text). Why: lets the work phase request a few VRAM writes without DMA setup.
In: vram_write_queue at $1C7B: pairs of words, address 0 ends.
Out: each pair written with VMADDL and VMDATAL; the first queue word is zeroed. S is moved to $1C7A for the PLA reads and restored by TXS; M restored.

blockNote: Actor scheduler, draw list sort, OAM builder, animation, combat and tile collision (file offsets 1445-4782, SNES $00:85A5-$92AD, bank 00).
=== ACTOR SLOTS ===

64 slots of $40 bytes at $0800 + $40 x n. Free slots sit on a stack at $1800-$187F (dp$4A points to it). Two links: run order is from actor_list_tail ($06A6) following $3E; the cull and sort pass goes from actor_list_head ($06A8) following $3C. A new actor is linked in as the new head.

Fields: $00 x, $02 y (words); $04 dx, $06 dy; $08 $0A $0C $0E extent box (left, top, right, bottom distances from x, y); $10 width, $12 height; $14 wait counter; $16 flags; $18 script resume address and $36 its bank; $1A attribute flags; $1C OAM attribute (bit 15 flip Y, bit 14 flip X); $1E animation id; $20 animation step; $22 animation table pointer; $24 data bank of the animation and spritemap data; $25 HP; $26 hit-stun counter; $28 spritemap pointer; $2C and $34 dynamic-tile bank and source; $2E $2F lair state copies; $30 projectile damage ($FF always kills); $38 meta entry pointer; $3A placement record pointer; $3C $3E links.
=== FLAGS ===

$16: $8000 off screen (set by CullAndSortActors and at spawn); $4000 pickup; $2000 hidden or inactive; $1000 runs tile collision; $0800 hit stun; $0400 dying; $0080 hit source (player side) or the player; $0020 projectile; $0010 runs during sub-frames; $0004 blocked by a tile; $0002 deflects hits; $0001 no enemy gauge. Read but unexplained: $0008, $0040, $0100, $0200 (OQ-I005-14).

$1A: $8000 dynamic-tile sprite; $4000 draw in front; $2000 draw behind; $0080 not drawn; $0040 frozen while stunned; $0100 survives lethal hits with 1 HP; $0200, $0400, $0800 immunity classes (special, metal, spirit; see COMBAT).
=== SCHEDULER ===

RunActors pushes EndRunActors - 1 and RunActorList - 1 and executes RTS: RunActorList starts with A = actor_list_tail, and when the list ends its RTS lands in EndRunActors, which restores dp$38-$3A, DBR and P and returns with RTL. RunActorList calls an actor script by pushing a bank-0 return address (StepActorMotion - 1), the script bank ($36) and $18 - 1, then RTL; the script returns with RTL into StepActorMotion with X = slot. A script runs when its wait counter $14 goes below 0. While subframe_active is set only actors with $16 bit $0010 run.
=== DRAW LIST ===

CullAndSortActors sets $16 bit $8000 for actors whose extent box misses the 256 x 224 screen and clears it for the rest, and builds the sorted draw list at $1900 (slot words, 0 ends). Key = (255 - (y - scroll_y)) x 2, so lower actors on screen sort first; key 0 for $1A bit $4000 (in front) and for actors with y - scroll_y outside 0-$FF; key $01FE for $1A bit $2000 (behind). Hidden ($16 bit $2000) and not-drawn ($1A bit $0080) actors are not listed. Bucket sort: pass 1 stores (key, slot) pairs at $1900, pass 2 pops them with S moved to $18FF into 256 linked buckets at $0100-$02FF (nodes carved from the OAM area at $0486), pass 3 pops the bucket heads with S = $00FF and writes the slots back to $1900 in key order, clearing every head with PHA/PLA (A = 0 over the popped word). The scan stops at the $FFFF end marker at $0300 (OQ-I013-1). S relocation is safe only because NMI is off in the work phase (OQ-I005-20).

BuildOamFromActors fills the OAM low table ($0486-$0685, 4 bytes per sprite: x, y, tile, attribute) and the high table ($0686-: two bits per sprite, x bit 8 and size) from the draw list through BuildActorSprites, until the list ends or all 128 sprites are used. Unused sprites are set to $E080 (off screen). A spritemap is a word entry count followed by 7-byte entries: flags (bit 0 = size bit), x offset, x offset when flipped in x, y offset, y offset when flipped in y, word tile and attribute (XOR $1C, or $0E00 while the stun flashes). Dynamic-tile actors ($1A bit $8000) copy tile blocks of 32 bytes at source + tile x 32 through tile_dma_list and use OAM tile numbers 0, 2, 4 and so on; the NMI uploads them.
=== ANIMATION ===

SetActorAnimFrame: $22 points to a word table indexed by the animation id; each entry points to a list of 8-byte steps indexed by $20: word duration (negative ends the animation), word dx, word dy, word frame pointer. A frame record has six words (left, right, top, bottom extents, width, height) followed at +12 by the spritemap. Flip bits of $1C negate dx and dy and mirror the extents.
=== COMBAT ===

DetectHitSourceCollisions pairs every listed actor with $16 bit $0080 (and none of $0D00) against every actor without $EEC0 whose box overlaps and whose sprite rectangles overlap (TestSpriteOverlap); sources with $16 bit $0020 go to ApplyProjectileHit, the others to ApplySwordHit. DetectPlayerContact tests the player's hurt box against actors without $25C0 and calls ApplyContactDamageOrPickup. The rules below are read from the code; the item names are those of the walkthrough (docs/walkthrough/items.md).

- Equipment ids: equipped_weapon $1B5E (2 Psycho Sword, 3 Critical Sword, 5 Zantetsu Sword, 6 Spirit Sword, 7 Recovery Sword, 8 Soul Blade), equipped_armor $1B60 ($0D Mystic Armor, $0E Light Armor), equipped_magic $1B62 ($18 Phoenix), equipped_bracelet $1B64 ($35 Power, $36 Shield, $37 Super).

- Sword damage = max(1, attack_current $1B8C - monster defence (meta entry +1)); Power and Super Bracelet double it. Monster HP is $25; a hit that does not leave HP above 0 kills (or leaves 1 HP when $1A bit $0100).

- Immunity classes ($1A): $0400 metal is hurt only by the Zantetsu Sword, $0800 spirit only by the Spirit Sword, $0200 special only by the Soul Blade (which hurts everything). Metal deflects with sound $4C, the other two ignore the hit silently.

- Damage to the player = max(1, monster attack - 1 - defense_current $1B8E); Shield and Super Bracelet halve it. Light Armor blocks the hit when attack x 1.5 is below $1B8E (sound $0C). Mystic Armor sets the hit stun counter to -64 instead of -32.
- Hit stun: $26 = -8 for monsters, $FFE0 or $FFC0 for the player; while $16 bit $0800 is set the stunned player only picks things up.
- Differences from the walkthrough are in OQ-I005-1 (Super Bracelet), -2 (Critical Sword), -3 (Psycho Sword).
=== COLLISION ===

MoveActorWithTileCollision moves x first (CollideEast or CollideWest), then y (CollideSouth or CollideNorth), each probing the tile types in the rows or columns the actor's width and height cover. GetTileType reads tile_type_map ($7F8000): index = ((y / 16) x map_width_pages + x / 16) x 256 + (y and 15) x 16 + (x and 15) for tile coordinates; a type byte with a high nibble set (Cop15_BlockOwnTiles ORs $F0) or an index of $4000 or more reads as $0F (blocked). Blocked: $00 or $02 snapped to a multiple of 16, velocity zeroed, $16 bit $0004 set. Tile type codes are in OQ-I005-8; the east and south routines have no boundary pre-check (OQ-I005-12).
=== ENEMY GAUGE ===

A hit on a monster without $16 bit $0001 sets enemy_gauge_hp ($0336) to its HP, enemy_gauge_max ($0338) to the meta entry HP (+2) and enemy_gauge_timer ($0330) to $80. The HUD update (code_012659) draws the gauge string asciistring_01476F ([04:336,338]) once, counts the timer down by 2 per frame and erases the gauge when it reaches 0.

partNotes.HandleIrq: IRQ vector: a bare RTI. The I flag is never cleared (no CLI in extracted/), so the IRQ stays masked even though NMITIMEN is written as $A1.
RunActors: When: every frame (8 call sites: the main loop variants, the sub-frames and the scene loader).
Sees: all enemy, NPC and effect behaviour advances one step.
Why: the engine is a cooperative scheduler: scripts yield with RTL.
Out: actor_run_count ($1F00) = actors visited; dp$38-$3A saved by PEI and restored by EndRunActors.
Clobbers: A, X, Y (P and DBR restored).
partNotes.EndRunActors: Landing point of RunActorList's closing RTS (the RTS trick of RunActors): restores dp$38-$3A, DBR and P and returns to RunActors' caller with RTL. Clobbers X.
CullAndSortActors: Marks which actors are off screen and builds the sorted draw list at $1900.
When: every frame after RunActors, and in each sub-frame.
Sees: actors nearer the bottom of the screen draw in front; off-screen actors cost nothing.
Why: OAM order decides sprite priority, so the list is sorted by screen y; the off-screen flag lets scripts such as CopAD wait for visibility (OQ-I005-11).
In: none (reads actor_list_head, scroll_bg1_x/y and the actor fields).
Out: $16 bit $8000 set or cleared; $1900 holds the slot words in key order, ended by 0 (keys in the block note). The $0200 compare before the key store is a dead guard: the key never exceeds $01FE.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, dp$00, dp$02; S relocated and restored; scratch: buckets $0100-$02FF (re-zeroed), nodes from $0486.
partNotes.CullNextActor: Loop head of pass 1: X = actor (0 ends, branch to FillSortBuckets); tests the extent box against the screen; the next actor comes from $3C.
partNotes.MarkActorOnScreen: Visible actor that is not listed (hidden or not drawn) or was listed: clear $16 bit $8000 and go to the next actor ($3C).
partNotes.MarkActorOffScreen: Actor box misses the screen: set $16 bit $8000 and go to the next actor ($3C).
partNotes.FillSortBuckets: Pass 2 of the sort: terminates the pair list with $FFFF, sets dp$02 = $0486 (next free node), moves S to $18FF and pushes every (key, slot) pair into the bucket for its key (new node in front of the old head).
partNotes.FlattenSortBuckets: Pass 3 of the sort: S = $00FF so PLY pops the 256 bucket heads in key order; each chain is written back to $1900 slot by slot.
partNotes.ClearBucketHead: End of a chain: PHA with A = 0 overwrites the bucket head just popped, PLA restores S. This is the bucket clear, done without a store loop.
partNotes.TerminateDrawList: End marker found: stores 0 as the last draw list word, restores S from dp$00 and P, returns with RTL.
BuildOamFromActors: Fills the OAM buffer from the draw list.
When: every frame, after CullAndSortActors, before the NMI copies the buffer.
Why: the NMI can only transfer a finished buffer; this builds it in priority order.
Out: oam_buffer low table ($0486-$0685) and high table ($0686-); unused sprites $E080 (off screen). Stops when the list ends or the buffer is full.
Clobbers: A, X, Y; dp$00, dp$02, dp$04 (tile record pointer, starts $1A06), dp$4C, dp$4E, dp$52, dp$54; DBR and P restored; S relocated.
partNotes.FillOamOffscreen: Writes $E080 (x $80, y $E0) into all 512 bytes of the low OAM table with 16 PHA per pass while S runs down from $0685: every sprite starts off screen.
partNotes.BuildOamLoop: Takes the next slot from the draw list (0 ends) and calls BuildActorSprites with X = slot; carry set means the OAM is full.
partNotes.FlushOamHighBits: Draw list ended: right-aligns the bits of the last, partial high-table byte (two shifts for every sprite still missing) and stores it at dp$4C.
BuildActorSprites: Emits the OAM entries of one actor from its spritemap.
When: once per listed actor per frame, from BuildOamLoop.
Sees: the actor's current animation frame, flipped, flashing or blinking while stunned.
Why: spritemaps are position-independent entries; this adds the screen position and the flips.
In: X = actor, Y = OAM byte offset (multiple of 4), dp$52 and dp$54 = scroll origin minus 16, dp$4C, dp$4E, dp$04, dp$02.

Out: one OAM entry per spritemap entry (entries clipped outside the screen get $E080); Y advanced; carry set when the OAM is full (Y = $0200). Dynamic-tile actors take BuildDynamicTileSprites. Stun counter $26: negative = palette 7 flash on alternate frames ($0E00 into dp$06), positive = not drawn on alternate frames (OQ-I023-1).
Clobbers: A, dp$00, dp$06, dp$0C, dp$16, dp$18, dp$50, $1A02, $1A04; X and DBR restored (DBR = $24 of the actor inside).
partNotes.BuildDynamicTileSprites: Dynamic-tile variant of BuildActorSprites ($1A bit $8000): reads the tile source from $34 and $2C, increments tile_dma_pending, and for each spritemap entry appends a 3-byte record (source + tile x 32, bank) to tile_dma_list through dp$04 and gives the entry the OAM tile number dp$02 (0, 2, 4 ...). The list ends with a 0 word.
SetActorAnimFrame: Loads the next animation step into the actor.
When: after an animation id change and at each step end (14 call sites: player code, COP handlers, spawn and the loader).
Sees: the next frame of the animation, with flips applied.
Why: one table drives duration, velocity, hit box and spritemap together.
In: X = actor; $1E animation id, $20 step, $22 table, $24 bank, $1C flip bits.

Out: carry clear = step loaded: $14 duration, $04 and $06 velocity (negated for flips), $28 spritemap pointer, $08-$0E extents (mirrored), $10, $12 size; $20 incremented. Carry set = end marker (see EndAnimation).
partNotes.EndAnimation: End marker (negative duration): $20 = 0, velocity $04 and $06 = 0, carry set, DBR restored.
partNotes.NextActor: Loads A = $3E of the current actor X (the next actor toward the head) and falls into RunActorList.
RunActorList: Runs the scripts of all actors from A to the head.
When: every frame, entered by the RTS trick of RunActors.
Sees: each actor acts on its own timer.
Why: handles hit stun, the sub-frame filter, wait counters and the script call in one loop.

Out: for each actor until A = 0: actor_run_count++; hit stun ($16 bit $0800): $26 counts up when negative and down when positive, the flag clears at 0, and the script is skipped while $1A bit $0040 is set; skips actors without $16 bit $0010 while subframe_active is set; $14 counts down and at 0 the script at $36:$18 runs with X = slot; then StepActorMotion. RTS into EndRunActors at the end.
partNotes.FilterSubFrameActor: While subframe_active is non-zero, an actor without $16 bit $0010 is skipped (go to NextActor).
partNotes.CountDownAndRunScript: Decrements the wait counter $14; while it is still 0 or above the actor goes straight to StepActorMotion. Otherwise it clears $14 and calls the script: pushes bank 0 and StepActorMotion - 1, then the script bank $36 and address $18 - 1, and RTL enters the script.
StepActorMotion: Return point of every actor script: moves the actor, then goes to the next one.
When: after each script yields (RTL), and for actors that did not run this frame.
Sees: actors slide by their velocity and stop at walls.
Why: movement and collision happen after the script has set $04 and $06.
Out: when $16 bit $1000 is set, MoveActorWithTileCollision runs; always ApplyActorVelocity; then NextActor.
DetectHitSourceCollisions: Finds which hit sources (the player's sword, magic and projectiles) touch which actors this frame.
When: every frame after the sort, in the main loop only.
Sees: monsters flash, are knocked back, lose HP and die.
Why: the draw list gives the on-screen candidates cheaply.
In: none; skipped when the player actor is dying ($16 bit $0400).

Out: for every listed actor with $16 bit $0080 and none of $0D00 (source), scans the list for targets without any of $EEC0 whose box overlaps; TestSpriteOverlap confirms; sources with $16 bit $0020 call ApplyProjectileHit, others ApplySwordHit. A source can hit several targets in one frame.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, dp$00-$06 (source box top, bottom, left, right), dp$3E (source slot); DBR and P restored.
partNotes.NextHitSource: Next source candidate from the draw list; 0 ends the scan. A source needs $16 bit $0080 and none of $0D00.
partNotes.LoadHitSourceBox: Loads the source's box into dp$00-$06 (top = y - $0A, bottom = y + $0E, left = x - $08, right = x + $0C) and sets the source slot in dp$3E; X restarts at the head of the list for the targets.
partNotes.NextHitTarget: Next target from the draw list; box overlap test against dp$00-$06, then TestSpriteOverlap, then the hit routines. 0 ends the targets of this source.
ApplySwordHit: Applies the equipped sword to a hit target: damage, freeze, immunity, kill and EXP.
When: a sword-side source ($16 bit $0080, not a projectile) overlaps a target.
Sees: the monster flashes and is knocked back, loses HP, or dies with a drop and EXP; deflected hits ring.
Why: all sword rules live here, so every weapon differs only by id (rules in the block note).
In: X = source, Y = target; ignored when the player animation $1E is $24 or more.
Out: target $25 (HP), $26, $16, $1A, $18, $36, $14; HUD bits in $0332; enemy gauge words; player_hp (Recovery Sword).
Clobbers: A, X; dp$00. Open: OQ-I005-1, -2, -3, -4.
partNotes.DeflectHit: BRK #$4C: sound $4C (the hit is deflected) and return without damage.
partNotes.CheckImmunityClass: Tests the $1A immunity classes: $0800 (spirit) needs weapon 6, $0400 (metal) needs weapon 5 and otherwise deflects, $0200 (special) ignores the hit (the Soul Blade skipped this earlier); no class goes on to ApplySwordDamage.
partNotes.ApplySwordDamage: Damage path: weapon 3 (Critical Sword) kills when (frame_counter and $0F) = 0 except the $039A actor; otherwise damage = max(1, attack_current - monster defence), doubled for the Super or Power Bracelet, subtracted from $25; HP 0 or below goes to KillOrSpareTarget, else the target is stunned ($26 = -8, $16 bit $0800), frozen while the player swings ($20-$23), and sound $42 plays.
partNotes.KillOrSpareTarget: Lethal hit: with $1A bit $0100 the target keeps 1 HP and takes the normal hit path, otherwise it is killed (KillTarget).
partNotes.KillTarget: Kills the target: script = code_002A10 (death and drops), HP 0, wait 0, $16 bit $0400 (dying); adds the meta entry EXP (+3) to the player EXP in BCD; HUD bit $0002; Recovery Sword (7) heals 1 HP (HUD bit $0004); sound $43.
partNotes.SetEnemyGauge: Unless $16 bit $0001: enemy_gauge_hp = target HP, enemy_gauge_max = meta entry HP (+2), enemy_gauge_timer = $80 (HUD gauge, see the block note).
ApplyProjectileHit: Applies a projectile (magic) hit to a target.
When: a projectile source ($16 bit $0020) overlaps a target.
Sees: the monster is hurt, stunned or killed by the spell.
Why: projectiles carry their own damage ($30) instead of using the sword formula.

Out: damage $30 ($FF = always kills) or, with equipped_magic $18 (Phoenix), $1B70 + $1B72 - defence; immunity checks as for the sword (metal deflects, spirit and special are ignored); stun $FFF8; kill as in KillTarget (no Recovery Sword).
partNotes.DeflectProjectile: BRK #$4C: sound $4C and return without damage.
partNotes.ApplyProjectileDamage: Damage = $30 of the projectile ($FF kills outright); subtracts it from the target HP; HP 0 or below goes to KillOrSpareProjectileTarget, otherwise StunProjectileTarget.
partNotes.ApplyPhoenixDamage: Phoenix equipped: damage = max(1, $1B70 + $1B72 - monster defence) instead of the projectile's $30.
partNotes.StunProjectileTarget: Stores the HP, sets the stun ($26 = $FFF8, $16 bit $0800), clears $1A bit $0040 and plays sound $42.
partNotes.KillOrSpareProjectileTarget: Lethal projectile hit: $1A bit $0100 keeps 1 HP, otherwise the target is killed as in KillTarget (script code_002A10, EXP, HUD bit $0002, sound $43).
partNotes.SetEnemyGaugeProjectile: Same as SetEnemyGauge for projectile hits.
TestSpriteOverlap: Exact hit test: does any spritemap rectangle of the source overlap the target's box?
When: after the coarse box test of DetectHitSourceCollisions.
Sees: hits land where sprites touch, not where boxes touch.
Why: boxes are coarse; spritemaps give the real shapes.
In: Y = target, dp$3E = source, dp$00-$06 = target box.
Out: carry set when any rectangle (size 8 or 16 by the entry flag bit 0, flips from $1C of the source) overlaps; X and Y preserved.
DetectPlayerContact: Finds actors touching the player and applies contact damage or pickups.
When: every frame after DetectHitSourceCollisions, main loop only.
Sees: the player takes damage or picks up items and drops.
Why: monsters hurt by touch, pickups work by touch.
In: none; skipped while contact_lock ($042D) is non-zero or the player is dying.

Out: hurt box x from x + 5 to x + 12, y from y - 12 to y - 4; scans the draw list for actors without any of $25C0 that overlap and calls ApplyContactDamageOrPickup until it returns carry clear; while the player is stunned ($16 bit $0800) only pickups ($16 bit $4000) are tested.
Clobbers: A, X, Y; dp$16, dp$18, dp$1A, dp$1C; P restored.
partNotes.NextContactCandidate: Next actor of the draw list for the contact scan; 0 ends. Actors with $25C0 are skipped.
partNotes.ScanContactPickups: Contact scan while the player is stunned: same box test, but only actors with $16 bit $4000 (pickups) count.
ApplyContactDamageOrPickup: A touching actor either gives its pickup or hurts the player.
When: DetectPlayerContact finds an overlapping actor.
Sees: items and drops are collected, or the player loses HP, flashes and is briefly invulnerable.
Why: all contact rules and armor effects are in one place (rules in the block note).

Out: pickups ($16 bit $4000): code_002F0A, carry set so the scan goes on. Otherwise damage = max(1, attack - 1 - $1B8E), halved with the Shield or Super Bracelet; Light Armor may block (sound $0C); player_hp reduced (floor 0), HUD bit $0004, player $26 = $FFC0 (Mystic Armor) or $FFE0, sound $04, stun flag. Carry clear.
MoveActorWithTileCollision: Moves an actor by its velocity with tile collision, x first, then y.
When: StepActorMotion for actors with $16 bit $1000 (and the player code).
Sees: actors stop at walls instead of walking through them.
Why: separate axes let an actor slide along a wall.
In: X = actor with $04 and $06; RTL.
Out: when ($10 or $12) has bit 3 the actor is tested with one point (ProbeTileAtVelocity); otherwise CollideEast for dx above 0, CollideWest for dx below 0, then CollideSouth or CollideNorth for dy.
CollideEast: East collision: blocks the actor when the tiles in front of it are walls.
In: X = actor, dx above 0. Out: carry set = blocked: $00 snapped to a multiple of 16, $04 = 0, $16 bit $0004 set; carry clear = free and the bit cleared.
Probes the rows covered by the height: the current column for type $0A, then the next column for $0F, $05, $06. No tile-boundary pre-check (OQ-I005-12); type codes OQ-I005-8.
Clobbers: A, dp$00, dp$0C, dp$0E, dp$16, dp$18, dp$1C.
partNotes.CollideWest: West collision, as CollideEast with a tile-boundary pre-check: current column type $05, next column $0F, $0A, $06; dx below 0 (OQ-I005-8, -12).
partNotes.CollideSouth: South collision, as CollideEast for y ($02 snapped, $06 = 0), no pre-check: current row type $0C, next row $0F, $03, $06; dy above 0.
partNotes.CollideNorth: North collision, as CollideSouth with a tile-boundary pre-check: current row type $03, next row $0F, $0C, $06; dy below 0.
ProbeTileAtVelocity: One-point tile test for small actors: stops the actor when the tile at its next position is blocked.

In: X = actor. Out: tile (x + dx - 4, y + dy - 4): type $0F zeroes $04 and $06, sets $16 bit $0004 and returns carry set; otherwise clears the bit, carry clear. Returns at once when dx is 0 (OQ-I005-9; the compare with $0F depends on the B byte, OQ-I005-10).
GetTileType: Returns the collision type of a map tile.
When: 17 call sites in the collision routines.
In: dp$16 = tile x (byte), dp$18 = tile y (word), M = 0 or 1.

Out: carry clear and A (8-bit) = low nibble of the tile when its high nibble is 0; carry set and A = $0F when the high nibble is non-zero (an actor blocks the tile, Cop15_BlockOwnTiles ORs $F0) or the index is $4000 or more. Index = ((y / 16) x map_width_pages + x / 16) x 256 + (y and 15) x 16 + (x and 15). The B byte is left stale (OQ-I005-10).
Clobbers: A; X and P preserved.
partNotes.ApplyActorVelocity: Adds the velocity to the position: $00 += $04 and $02 += $06 (16-bit). In: X = actor. Clobbers A.

1466.text: RTS enters RunActorList with A = actor_list_tail; its closing RTS returns into EndRunActors

1502.text: Screen test: 256 wide ($0100), 224 high ($00E0), using the extent box ($08 left, $0A top, $0C right, $0E bottom)

1565.text: Hidden ($16 bit $2000) or not drawn ($1A bit $0080): on screen but not put in the draw list

1608.text: key = (255 - (y - scroll_y)) x 2: the lower an actor stands, the smaller the key; ascending keys, OAM index 0 is in front

1617.text: Pass 1: (key, slot) pairs at $1900, 4 bytes each, in list order

1631.text: Clear the off-screen flag $8000 (set means off screen, OQ-I005-11)

1658.text: End of pass 1: key $FFFF ends the pair list

1664.text: Pass 2 (bucket sort): dp$02 = next free node, carved from the OAM area at $0486 (BuildOamFromActors overwrites it later)

1669.text: S moved to $18FF so PLX and PLA pop the pairs from $1900 upward; old S waits in dp$00 (safe only with NMI off)

1679.text: Bucket head for this key: 256 words at $0100-$02FF; nodes are (slot, next) and a new node goes in front

1734.text: Pass 3: S = $00FF so PLY pops the 256 bucket heads in key order

1743.text: A = 0 here (end of a chain): PHA overwrites the head word just popped, PLA restores S: the bucket clear without a store loop

1748.text: A negative word ends the scan: the $FFFF end marker at $0300 (OQ-I013-1)

1766.text: Zero ends the sorted draw list

1780.text: dp$04 = tile record pointer (tile_dma_list); the first record is emptied below

1794.text: dp$52, dp$54 = scroll origin minus 16: sprites may start up to 16 pixels off screen

1808.text: dp$4C = OAM high table pointer, dp$4E = sprites left in the current byte (4, two bits each)

1821.text: S relocated to the end of the OAM low table: the PHA loop writes $E080 words, every sprite starts off screen (Y = $E0)

1857.text: Next slot of the sorted draw list; 0 ends it

1878.text: Last, partial high-table byte: right-align the bits (two shifts per missing sprite) and store it

1893.text: DBR = the actor's data bank ($24) for the spritemap reads

1910.text: dp$16, dp$18 = screen x and y of the spritemap origin (position - extent left or top - scroll origin)

1924.text: dp$50 = flip bits of $1C: bit 15 flips Y, bit 14 flips X

1939.text: Stun counter $26: negative = palette 7 flash on alternate frames; positive = not drawn on alternate frames (blink, OQ-I023-1)

2044.text: High table bits: x bit 8 (from the position sum), then the size bit (spritemap flags bit 0); four sprites fill a byte

2056.text: Four sprites collected: store the high-table byte and advance

2098.text: Dynamic-tile sprites: $34 = tile source address, $2C = bank; each tile number picks a 32-byte block there for the NMI to copy

2301.text: Animation id selects an entry of the word table at $22; the entry points to a list of 8-byte steps indexed by $20

2324.text: Negative duration = end marker (EndAnimation: step 0, velocity 0, carry set)

2335.text: ROL: carry = bit 15 (flip Y), sign = bit 14 (flip X); flips negate the velocity and mirror the extents

2509.text: Hit stun ($16 bit $0800): $26 counts toward 0 (up when negative, down when positive); at 0 the flag clears

2553.text: Sub-frame filter: while subframe_active is set only actors with $16 bit $0010 run

2566.text: $14 = wait counter; the script runs when it goes below 0

2579.text: Script call by RTL: bank 0 and StepActorMotion - 1 are pushed first, then the script bank $36 and address $18 - 1

2622.text: Player dying ($16 bit $0400): no hits this frame

2651.text: Source needs $0080 (hits other actors) and none of $0D00 (hit stun, dying, bit $0100)

2719.text: Target must have none of $EEC0 (off screen, pickup, hidden, hit stun, dying, hit source, $0200, $0040)

2779.text: $16 bit $0020 = projectile source; all others are sword hits

2808.text: Sword hits count only while the player animation ($1E) is below $24

2817.text: $16 bit $0002: this actor deflects every hit

2822.text: BRK #n requests sound n (the BRK handler stores it in sound_request); $4C = deflected hit

2825.text: equipped_weapon: 8 (Soul Blade) skips every immunity check

2836.text: Weapon 2 (Psycho Sword): a target with an immunity class ($1A bits $0E00), except the $039A actor, is frozen for 180 frames (OQ-I005-3)

2878.text: Immunity classes in $1A: $0800 spirit (Spirit Sword 6 only), $0400 metal (Zantetsu Sword 5 only, others deflect), $0200 special (Soul Blade only)

2917.text: Weapon 3 (Critical Sword): when (frame_counter and $0F) = 0 the hit kills outright, except the $039A actor (OQ-I005-2)

2946.text: damage = max(1, attack_current ($1B8C) - monster defence (meta entry +1))

2977.text: Target HP - damage; zero or below goes to the kill path

3000.text: Player animation $20-$23 (sword swing): the target stays frozen ($1A bit $0040) during the stun; otherwise the bit is cleared

3028.text: Hit stun: $26 = -8 (counts up to 0) and $16 bit $0800

3052.text: $1A bit $0100: survives a lethal hit with 1 HP

3063.text: Kill: script = code_002A10 (death and drops), HP 0, wait 0, $16 bit $0400 (dying)

3099.text: EXP = meta entry +3, added to the player EXP in BCD by code_027687

3113.text: Weapon 7 (Recovery Sword): +1 HP per kill (HUD HP bit)

3154.text: Enemy gauge for the HUD: $0336 = HP after the hit, $0338 = max HP (meta +2), $0330 = $80 starts the display timer

3194.text: equipped_magic $18 (Phoenix): damage from the attack formula below instead of $30

3575.text: contact_lock non-zero: no player contact this frame

3590.text: Player hurt box: dp$16, dp$1A = x + 5, x + 12; dp$18, dp$1C = y - 12, y - 4

3621.text: Player in hit stun: only pickups are tested (ScanContactPickups)

3639.text: Skip actors with $25C0 (hidden, dying, $0100, hit source, $0040)

3677.text: Carry clear = damage applied, stop. Carry set (pickup, or nothing) keeps scanning

3744.text: Pickup actor ($16 bit $4000): handled by code_002F0A, carry set

3749.text: equipped_armor: $0E (Light Armor) blocks the hit when monster attack x 1.5 is below defense_current (sound $0C)

3787.text: damage = attack (meta entry +0) - 1 - defense_current ($1B8E), at least 0 here

3845.text: Mystic Armor ($1B60 = $0D): stun counter -64 instead of -32 (longer invulnerability)

3886.text: Width or height with bit 3 set: one-point test (ProbeTileAtVelocity) instead of the box

4619.text: Reads $04 twice (probably meant $04 or $06): returns only when dx is 0 (OQ-I005-9)

4661.text: Type $0F blocks; the 16-bit compare relies on the B byte being 0 (OQ-I005-10)

4700.text: y x 16: low byte = (y and 15) x 16 (row in the page), high byte = y / 16 (page row)

4737.text: An index of $4000 or more is outside the type map: blocked ($0F)

4748.text: High nibble set = tile blocked by an actor (Cop15_BlockOwnTiles ORs $F0): reads as $0F

blockNote: Actor spawning, then lair, death and drop scripts (file offsets 4783-5393 are batch A1, SNES $00:92AF-$94D1; the scripts from code_0026F3 on belong to batch A2 and are not described here).
=== SPAWN PIPELINE (A1 part) ===

Scene load (the scene loader) calls InitActorPool (free-slot stack and pool cleared) and SpawnSceneActors, then the lair code spawns the lair actors. SpawnSceneActors reads world_index ($03BA) and sets $03B0 = offset of the world's meta list inside meta_tables_008000 (the table starts with one list pointer per world, seven in all); it finds the first 4-byte record of table_0099B4 whose area and scene match (the table ends at a first byte of $80 or more) and calls SpawnPlacementList once.

SpawnPlacementList reads 4-byte placement records (bank $01) until a $FF record, allocates an actor for each (code_00668A), links it as the new head and calls InitActorFromPlacement. The actor with $16 bit $0080 is the player: it is placed at warp_dest_x and warp_dest_y + 16 when they are non-zero (anim warp_dest_anim), warp_dest_* are cleared, and player_tile_x/y, player_x/y and player_actor are set.
=== STRUCTURES ===
Placement record (4 bytes, bank $01): x tile, y tile, flags byte (bits 7 and 6 flip Y and X, bit 0 passes to $1C as $0100), meta type. Position = tile x 16, tile y x 16 + 16.

Meta entry (14 bytes at meta_tables_008000 + $03B0 + type x 14): +0 attack, +1 defence, +2 HP, +3 word EXP, +5 animation id, +6 word flags (becomes $16, $8000 added at spawn), +8 word animation table, +A data bank, +B word script, +D script bank.

Lair record (32 bytes in data_00BA0D, see its note): used by SpawnLairActor: +$C x tile, +$D y tile, +$10 script word, +$12 script bank, +$13 monster count (initial lair state), +$14 spawn interval or formation index, +$15 meta type, +$16 attribute word.
=== NOTES ===

- Names: the lair actor (SpawnLairActor) is the invisible object that runs the lair script and counts the monsters left in $2E and $2F; the monsters it spawns are made by the scripts that follow (batch A2).
- A Monster Lair in the walkthrough loses its shield when its monsters are dead and shows a green switch; the tile $FE written by the lair code is that switch (see lib_scene_map_patches).

InitActorPool: Resets the actor pool: free-slot stack, list tail and all slots.
When: once per scene load (the scene loader).
Sees: nothing directly; every actor of the old scene is gone.
Why: each scene starts with an empty pool.
Out: $1800-$187F = the 64 slot addresses ($0800, $0840, ... $17C0); dp$4A = $1800; actor_list_tail = $0800; $0800-$17FF zeroed.
SpawnSceneActors: Finds the actor placement list of the current scene and spawns it.
When: once per scene load, after InitActorPool.
Sees: the monsters, NPCs, chests and the player of the new scene appear.
Why: every scene's actors are listed in table_0099B4 by area and scene.
Out: $03B0 = offset of the world's meta list in meta_tables_008000; SpawnPlacementList called for the first matching record.
SpawnPlacementList: Creates one actor per 4-byte placement record and places the player.
When: from SpawnSceneActors, once per scene.
Why: records carry only position, flags and a meta type; this expands them.
In: X = offset of the table_0099B4 record (M = 1 on entry).

Out: dp$29-$2B = long pointer to the placement records (bank $01); each actor allocated, linked as new head ($3E of the old head, $3C of the new one), record pointer in $3A, filled by InitActorFromPlacement; ends at the $FF record. Player: position from warp_dest_x and warp_dest_y + 16 when non-zero, animation from warp_dest_anim, warp_dest cleared, player_tile_x/y, player_x/y, player_actor set; actor_list_head set for each new actor.
partNotes.NextPlacement: Reads the next placement record byte: $FF ends the list (RTS); otherwise allocates the next actor and links it in front of the previous one.
InitActorFromPlacement: Fills a new actor from its placement record and its meta entry.
When: once per placed actor (SpawnPlacementList and the COP spawn handler cop_handler_005CF0).
Sees: the actor starts with the right position, graphics, HP and script.
Why: the meta entry holds the per-monster-type data (attack, defence, HP, EXP, animation, script).
In: X = new slot, $3A,X = record pointer in bank $01.

Out: position = tile x 16 and tile y x 16 + 16; $1C = record bits $C100 or $0372; meta entry = $03B0 + type x 14: $38 pointer, $25 HP (+2), $1E animation (+5), $24 bank (+A), $36 script bank (+D), $16 flags (+6) or $8000, $22 animation table (+8), $18 script (+B); extents from SetActorAnimFrame, or a 16x16 box for actors with $16 bit $2000 and not $0040; $14, $04, $06 = 0.
Clobbers: A, X (= slot on return), Y.
SpawnLairActor: Creates the actor of one Monster Lair.
When: at scene load, for every lair of the location whose state byte is positive (monsters left).
Sees: nothing by itself (the actor is hidden); its script releases the lair's monsters, and when they are all dead the lair opens (green switch).
Why: a lair is a script actor with a monster counter: lair_state survives scene changes and the actor is rebuilt from it.
In: X = lair index (byte table $7F0203), Y = lair record offset in data_00BA0D (32 bytes per record).

Out: new actor allocated before the head (code_006662), $16 = $A000 (off screen and hidden), $34 = lair index, position (+$C x 16, (+$D + 1) x 16), $1C and $30 = (+$16 or $0100 or $0372), script $18 (+$10) and $36 (+$12), $2E and $2F = lair state byte, $26 = +$14, meta entry from +$15 ($38, $25, $1E, $24, $22), size and extents 16, $32 = 0.
Clobbers: A, X, Y restored; P restored.

4786.text: Free-slot stack at $1800-$187F: 64 words, one slot address each ($0800 + n x $40); dp$4A points to it

4838.text: meta_tables_008000 starts with one list pointer per world (indexed by world_index, $03BA)

4853.text: table_0099B4: 4-byte records (area, scene, pointer to the placement list); a first byte of $80 or more ends the table

4886.text: dp$29-$2B = long pointer to the placement records (bank $01)

4917.text: Link: the old actor's $3E = new slot (toward the head), the new actor's $3C = old (toward the tail)

4954.text: warp_dest_x and warp_dest_y both 0: keep the placement position

4969.text: +16, as in InitActorFromPlacement (position y = tile y x 16 + 16)

5039.text: Placement record (bank $01): x tile, y tile, flags byte, meta type

5073.text: Flags word: $C000 (flips) and $0100 pass to $1C; the default attribute $0372 is ORed in

5091.text: type x 14: entry size of meta_tables_008000; $03B0 (list offset of this world) is added next

5136.text: $8000 set: the actor starts flagged off screen until the first CullAndSortActors

5168.text: Hidden actors without $0040: no animation, a 16x16 default box (size and extents set directly)

5205.text: State byte of this lair ($7F0203 + lair index), copied to $2E and $2F below

5211.text: Position from the lair record: x = +$C tile x 16, y = (+$D tile + 1) x 16

5245.text: $16 = $A000: off screen and hidden; the lair actor is invisible and only runs its script

5280.text: Script address from lair record +$10, script bank from +$12

5296.text: $2E and $2F = the state byte (monsters left); a child's death decrements $2E of the parent

5304.text: $26 = lair record +$14: spawn interval or formation index, used by the lair scripts

5315.text: Meta entry from lair record +$15 (type x 14 + $03B0): HP, animation, bank and table; extents are 16

blockNote: Code that nothing in the ROM calls (file offsets 517-833 and 29873-29906, bank 00).
=== DEBUG BLOCK (offsets 517-833, SNES $00:8205-$8341) ===

DebugPollPad2 and its helpers have no caller and no vector entry: a pad 2 poll (Select: scan banks $00, $03, $04 and $1F for the bytes 02 01 AA followed by a word of $8000 or more; B: wait 30 frames; Y: show a hex position readout), a hex digit helper pair and table, and DebugApplyItem (a two-digit BCD item entry in $0484 that nothing writes). They look like leftover debug code; that is an inference, not proven (OQ-I005-22 asks for a CDL run). us/overrides.json forces M = 1 at offsets 517 and 797.

DebugShowPosition writes hex digits into the text buffer $1F06-$1F1A (area, scene, location, tile x, x low digit, tile y, y low digit, actor count) and prints it from $1F02 through the text renderer code_012769; the template at $1F02-$1F05 is never initialised.

An unreferenced actor script: it waits with COP 80 and COP 82 until $0482 = 4, repeats the wait, runs COP 80/82 for ids 08 and 09, increments $0482 and ends with COP 91. It is not part of batch A1 and is left unnamed.

DebugPollPad2: When: never; no reference exists in the ROM.
Sees: nothing in the shipped game.
Why: probably a developer hook (inference, OQ-I005-22).
Out: Select on pad 2 runs DebugScanBanks; B waits 30 frames; Y runs DebugShowPosition.
Clobbers: A, X, Y; reads JOY2H ($421B).
partNotes.DebugScanBanks: Calls DebugScanBank for banks $00, $03, $04 and $1F (never called).
partNotes.DebugScanBank: Scans $8000-$FFFF of the bank in A for the bytes 02 01 AA followed by a word of $8000 or more and calls code_012C27 with $03F3 = $040A for each hit; purpose unknown (OQ-I023-4). In: A = bank. DBR restored. Clobbers: A, X, Y, $03F3.
partNotes.DebugShowPosition: Writes area, scene, location, tile x, x low digit, tile y, y low digit and the actor count as hex digits into $1F06-$1F1A, prints the buffer from $1F02 with code_012769 and sets vram_upload_flags = 1 (never called). Clobbers: A, X, Y.
partNotes.DebugHexHighNibble: High nibble of A (four LSR) as an ASCII hex digit; falls into DebugHexLowNibble. In: A (8-bit). Out: A = ASCII.
partNotes.DebugHexLowNibble: Low nibble of A as an ASCII hex digit through DebugHexDigits; M = 1 on exit (B holds the next table byte). Clobbers: A, X.
partNotes.DebugHexDigits: The bytes 0123456789ABCDEF, indexed by a nibble.
partNotes.DebugApplyItem: Converts the two BCD digits in $0484 to a binary entry number (high digit x 10 + low digit through code_0131D1), stores that inventory entry with code_0120F9 and clears $0484. Nothing writes $0484 (never called). M = 1 on exit. Clobbers: A, B.
